overview.description: Ace-To-Six Lowball is a lowball variant in which aces are low, but straights and flushes count against the hand.
overview.deck: Standard 52-card deck (some tables allow one joker as a bug)

history.origins: Ace-to-six lowball developed in home games on the eastern United States and in London and European poker circles as a stricter lowball form.
timeline: 20th century: London and European rooms adopt ace-to-six low ranking.
Modern mixed games: Ace-to-six appears in specialist lowball and dealer's choice rotations.
history.evolution: Compared with ace-to-five, this form penalizes accidental straights and flushes, making low draws more demanding.
history.cultural: Known as a traditional lowball format in London-style mixed poker.

setup.players: Two to eight players. As in other five-card draw lowball games; deal and betting follow the same structure as California lowball. With more than six players the deck can run short on the draw and house rules may allow shuffling the muck for replacement cards.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck; optional joker bug in some house rules.
setup.equipment: Deck, chips, dealer button, and blind markers if blind structure is used.
setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards face-down to each player.

rules.objective: Make the lowest five-card hand by ace-to-six ranking.
rules.gameplay: Players contribute forced bets (ante or blinds), receive five down cards, complete first betting, perform a single draw (discard 0-5 then draw equal replacements, or stand pat), complete final betting, and go to showdown.
keyRules: Straights and flushes count and are bad for low ranking.
A-2-3-4-5 is a straight and therefore weak in this variant.
Hands are compared from highest card downward among low hands.

strategy.basic: Avoid draws that can complete a straight or flush by accident.
strategy.intermediate: Track outs that spoil lows, especially 5-completions to A-2-3-4 patterns.
strategy.advanced: Use pat lines selectively, since opponents also account for straight/flush contamination risk.
tips: A-2-3 starts can be awkward if they force straight-prone continuation cards.
A pat hand can be value or bluff depending on prior draw pattern.

list.name: Single Draw
list.description: One draw round and two main betting rounds.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Base engine already models the single-draw structure; no separate overrides are required.

list.name: Triple Draw
list.description: Three draw rounds with additional betting rounds.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Triple-draw format is described in sources, but detailed multi-draw engine overrides are not yet modeled.

difficulty.easy: Plays mostly by immediate hand value and simple draw choices.
difficulty.medium: Uses draw-count reads and basic pat-versus-draw inference.
difficulty.hard: Balances value and bluff lines from draw history and betting texture.

considerations: Evaluator must rank by ace-to-six low rules.
AI should model information from number of cards each opponent draws.

phases.label: Initial Deal
phases.notes: Deal five cards face-down to each player.

phases.label: Draw
phases.notes: Players may discard and draw replacements, or stand pat.

phases.label: Showdown
phases.notes: Reveal remaining hands and award pot to best low hand.

deal.description: Dealer distributes five private cards to each player.

reveal_market.reason: Ace-to-six lowball has no market; cards are dealt and drawn from stock only.

buy_market.reason: Draw poker; players receive cards by deal and draw, not by buying from a market.

buy_stock.reason: Cards are drawn in the draw phase via draw action, not a separate buy_stock action.

fold.description: Surrender claim to the current pot.

check.constraints: Only when no bet is currently open.

call.constraints: Only when a bet or raise is open.

bet.constraints: Only when no bet has been opened this round.

raise.constraints: Only when a bet is already open.

declare.reason: Poker variant; no high-low declaration phase, showdown decides winner.

reveal_hand.description: Expose cards at showdown for low-hand comparison.

award_pot.description: Award pot to the best ace-to-six low hand.

play_card.reason: Draw poker; players do not play cards to a trick, they hold hands to showdown.

draw.constraints: During draw phase only; card count drawn equals cards discarded.

discard.description: Discard selected card(s) to receive replacements.
discard.constraints: During draw phase only; may discard zero when standing pat.

pass.reason: Betting uses check/call/bet/raise; pass is a trick-taking concept, not used here.

bid.reason: Poker uses bet/call/raise; bid refers to contract bidding in trick games.

meld.reason: Ace-to-six lowball is poker, not rummy; there is no melding of sets or runs.

go_out.reason: Game ends at showdown when all betting is complete; no go-out-to-win mechanic.

notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Standard 52-card deck; no card has special action or bonus value.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Poker hand game; goal is best hand at showdown, not emptying hand.

edgeCases.text: A player may stand pat by drawing zero cards during draw phase.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers are used; aces count low in ace-to-six lowball.
engine.suitDescription: Four suits in the French tradition: spades (piques), hearts (cœurs), diamonds (carreaux), and clubs (trèfles). Each suit contains thirteen cards; suits do not affect hand rank in lowball.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks in each suit: ace (low), king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, and two. In ace-to-six, straights and flushes do count against the low hand.
engine.dealPattern: Five cards down, one draw round, showdown.

synthesis.shortDescription: Draw lowball where aces are low and straights/flushes count against your low hand.

prompts.human: Ace-to-six lowball: build the lowest hand while avoiding straights and flushes.
prompts.ai: Game: Ace-To-Six Lowball. Flow: forced bet, deal 5 down, bet, draw, bet, showdown. Rank by ace-to-six low with straights/flushes counting.

scoring.description: Pot game; best low hand wins the pot at showdown.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest valid ace-to-six hand at showdown wins.
scoring.splitRules: Exact ties split pot evenly with odd chip by house rule.

nullReasons.targetScore: Pot game; no fixed target score; play ends at showdown.
nullReasons.cardValues: Ace-to-six lowball is a pot poker game; hands are compared by lowball ranking, not by per-card point values.
